title: Man agreed to be killed and eaten then allowed penis to be cut off and fed to him - NewsBreak
text:
By Edward Easton Jane Lavender ,
44 minutes ago To the residents of the small German hamlet of Wüsterfeld, Armin Meiwes appeared to be an ordinary neighbor. He maintained a neat home, regularly trimmed his lawn, and seldom stirred up trouble.
However, within the confines of his timber-framed abode, the computer technician was harboring a fantasy so sinister it would later send shockwaves around the globe.
• Woman, 27, gang raped, stabbed 50 times and forced to carry her intestines in hands
• Model wife killed, castrated and cooked husband before eating him with BBQ sauce
Meiwes, hailing from Rotenburg, confessed to having been consumed by the thought of murdering and consuming another person since his youth.
He later suggested that this obsession took root during visits to slaughterhouses and butcher shops, where he developed a morbid fascination with the process.
During his teenage years, he even contemplated asking peers if he could amputate and consume parts of their bodies, refraining only out of fear of social ostracization.
Years down the line, the advent of the internet provided him with access to clandestine fetish forums where users graphically discussed cannibalism.
It was in these online spaces that he encountered Bernd Brandes, a 43-year-old engineer based in Berlin, reports the Mirror .
After weeks of explicit online correspondence, the duo reached a macabre agreement. Brandes would journey to Meiwes' residence and willingly submit to being murdered and eaten.
In exchange, Meiwes would amputate Brandes' penis, and they would attempt to consume it together. Brandes made the trip in March 2001.
Brandes consented to ingest sleeping pills and alcohol before Meiwes severed his penis with a knife.
The flesh was then cooked in a pan and served, although subsequent reports indicated that neither man managed to fully consume it.
The entire gruesome event was meticulously documented on film by Miewes.
As Brandes grew weaker from blood loss, he was ultimately stabbed to death.
Meiwes then dismembered the body, suspending parts on meat hooks and preserving large portions in a freezer next to ordinary food.
Over the next 10 months, he gradually defrosted and prepared the flesh, consuming an estimated 20 kilograms.
Investigators later revealed Meiwes approached the meals almost like solitary dinner parties. He used his finest cutlery, lit candles and drank red wine.
When questioned about how he felt eating his victim, he delivered nine words that shocked detectives: "With every bite, my memory of him grew stronger."
The case sparked legal chaos in Germany, where cannibalism itself wasn't a specific crime. Meiwes was initially convicted of manslaughter, but following a retrial was found guilty of murder for sexual gratification.
He remains imprisoned, his crime still considered one of the most disturbing in modern European history.
